Defined in: [controllers/format-for-aria.ts:59](https://github.com/TanStack/hotkeys/blob/main/packages/lit-hotkeys/src/controllers/format-for-aria.ts#L59)

A Lit ReactiveController whose `format` is `formatForAria` with the
controller's `platform` option, or the detected platform without one. A
`platform` passed to `format` wins. Use its value for `aria-keyshortcuts`
with Lit's `ifDefined`, so Lit omits the attribute for a multi-step
sequence, no hotkey, or a hotkey that can't fire right now (one that is
disabled, in a suspended scope, a suspended character key, or not
registered). The host updates when a registration changes.

Physical bindings such as `[KeyQ]` name the key the user presses in
Chromium browsers, once the keyboard layout has loaded. The host updates
when the layout loads or changes. A `layoutMap` passed to `format` wins.

Lit has no provider, so the options are the only defaults. Pass a getter to
read them from host properties.

## Example

```ts
class SearchButton extends LitElement {
  private formatForAria = new FormatForAriaController(this)

  render() {
    return html`
      <button aria-keyshortcuts=${ifDefined(this.formatForAria.format('Mod+K'))}>
        Search
      </button>
    `
  }
}
```

## Properties

### format

```ts
format: (hotkey, options) => string | undefined;
```

Defined in: [controllers/format-for-aria.ts:70](https://github.com/TanStack/hotkeys/blob/main/packages/lit-hotkeys/src/controllers/format-for-aria.ts#L70)

Formats a hotkey for `aria-keyshortcuts`, with the controller's platform
and the user's keyboard layout filled in. It takes the same options as
`formatForAria` and needs no `this`, so it can be passed around.

Formats a hotkey for an `aria-keyshortcuts` attribute so screen readers can
announce the shortcut. `Mod+K` becomes `Meta+K` on macOS and `Control+K`
elsewhere.

Modifiers use the ARIA names (`Control`, `Alt`, `Shift`, `Meta`) and come
before the key. Keys use `KeyboardEvent.key` values, such as `K`, `/`,
`Escape`, or `ArrowUp`, with `Space` for the space bar and `Plus` for the
plus key. A physical binding names the key at that position, so `[KeyQ]`
becomes `Q`, or the key from `layoutMap` such as `A` on a French AZERTY
keyboard. Logical punctuation stays as written, so `'?'` stays `?` even
where it takes Shift to type.

Returns `undefined` when the hotkey has no ARIA form, so the attribute is
omitted. This applies to empty or `null` hotkeys, multi-step sequences,
standalone modifiers, and physical codes with no key value such as
`[NumpadMemoryAdd]`. A one-step sequence formats like its chord.

For a control with two shortcuts, join both formatted values with a space.
In a server-rendered app, use your adapter's formatter or pass `platform`.
Without a `platform` option, `formatForAria` uses `'linux'` on the server,
like `formatForDisplay`.

#### Parameters

##### hotkey

`DisplayHotkey` \| `null` \| `undefined`

A hotkey string, raw object, parsed chord, or nothing

##### options?

`FormatAriaOptions` = `{}`

The platform and keyboard layout

#### Returns

`string` \| `undefined`

The attribute value, or `undefined` when there is none

#### Example

```ts
formatForAria('Mod+K', { platform: 'mac' }) // 'Meta+K'
formatForAria('Mod+Shift+P', { platform: 'windows' }) // 'Control+Shift+P'
formatForAria('Shift+Space') // 'Shift+Space'
formatForAria(['G', 'H']) // undefined
```
